messages:
jess: Canary rollout r-123 is spiking 5xxs and p95 latency doubled. Can we do a fast revert? worried about KV cache and sticky sessions — need a short checklist and an owner.
ops-bot: Alert: canary r-123 error_rate > 3% for 3m (rule: canary-error-high).
deploy-bot: Canary r-123 deployment at 2026-05-12T09:45Z reported elevated 502 count.
kai: Propose fast plan: 1) gate traffic (set canary -> 0%) 2) disable canary rollout in control plane 3) soft-invalidate canary KV prefix 4) scale down canary pods / instances 5) watch session drain & metrics. I'll take steps 1-2 now unless someone objects.
maria: +1. Before flip, snapshot perf dashboards and save recent traces/logs (important for postmortem). Link to runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/rollout-revert
alan: KV caveat: hard invalidation can break session affinity if tokens are stored under canary prefix. Suggest soft invalidate: bump prefix version or set small TTL, do background sweep instead of immediate purge. Example:
```
# soft invalidation request
curl -X POST "https://kv.internal/api/v1/invalidate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KV_TOKEN" -d '{"prefix":"canary/r-123/","mode":"soft"}'
```
This marks keys stale without dropping active sessions.
chris: Also watch routing quotas — if stable cannot absorb the full 100% we should enable traffic-hold on incoming client tier or spin up extra capacity. Keep an eye on per-route token quota and the p99 hotspot metrics.
devex-bot: Rollout control available in Console -> Rollouts -> r-123. Quick toggle: "Disable canary" (requires 2 confirmations). API: POST /v1/rollouts/r-123/traffic.
kai: Running step 1: setting traffic split to 0 for canary. Will post curl I used.
kai: ```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.com/v1/rollouts/r-123/traffic" 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"splits":{"canary":0,"stable":100}}'
```
kai: DONE — API returned 200. Traffic shows shifting to stable. monitoring now.
ops-bot: Alert: canary error_rate has decreased to 0.2% (auto-check).
jess: Seeing traffic shift in console, latency returning to baseline. Maria — I saved traces and exported the dashboard CSV.
maria: Nice. Add a note in the rollout event: "fast revert due to 502 spike; soft KV invalidate scheduled."
alan: I'll run soft invalidate in 30s and start a background sweep for the canary prefix to avoid stale mixing.
alan: ```
# kick off background sweep
curl -X POST "https://kv.internal/api/v1/sweep" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KV_TOKEN" -d '{"prefix":"canary/r-123/","concurrency":4}'
```
chris: Stable autoscaler picked up extra load fine, no quota throttles. Keep watching quotas for the next 15m. If p95 creeps back up, fallback to traffic-hold plan.
kai: I'll disable the canary rollout object in the control plane (prevent reenqueuing).
kai: DONE — rollout marked disabled.
devex-bot: UI event logged: user=kai action=disable_canary rollout=r-123.
ops-bot: Incident note: r-123 reverted via traffic split at 1935678922.
jess: Verified 10m baseline. No user-facing errors in SLO window. Good job team. Who's owning the postmortem?
maria: I'll start the postmortem draft and include KV decision notes + timeline.
kai: I'll write up the steps I ran and attach commands/snippets.
alan: Will include the soft invalidate details and the sweep logs.
chris: I'll add quota/scale telemetry.
jess: Thanks all :thumbsup: keeping watch for 30 more minutes then closing the incident.
ops-bot: Alert cleared: canary error rule resolved.
